messages:
Priya R: Quick follow-up from the RFC — we need a clear decision on how to attribute tokens when a single streaming completion hits multiple model fallbacks and tool calls. Current logs are ambiguous and finance had a couple of customer queries.
Sam L: Can you sketch the worst-case flow you want accounted for? e.g., stream -> tool-call -> fallback to smaller model -> continue streaming?
Priya R: Exactly. Example: user starts chat -> model A streams first 200 tokens, then we invoke tool X (metadata tokens ~30), model A hits OOM and we fall back to model B which streams remaining 800 tokens. Billing should reflect who produced what, and audit log must let us reconstruct per-token provenance.
Kenji: Today we write a single billing event with aggregated tokens and model list. That's not sufficient for per-token audits.
Zoe: Two orthogonal requirements: (1) accurate customer billing (they care about unit pricing/machine class) (2) internal auditability / ability to reconstruct. We can optimize for 2 and compress for 1.
Tam: My thought: emit fine-grained events during processing but coalesce at the ledger-ingest boundary. Ledger keeps an append-only view for audits (raw_events) and a compacted billing view used by finance.
Marta: Real question: what is the unique id we use to stitch? request_id is not enough when retries/handshakes create multiple child requests.
Priya R: Proposal: introduce a provenance vector for each token-chunk: provenance_id (uuid), parent_provenance_ids (list), source_type (model/tool), model_name, token_count, start_token_index, end_token_index. We append these as individual 'provenance records' during runtime and checkpoint them to the raw_events stream.
Sam L: That solves stitching but increases event cardinality massively for long responses. We need bounding: either chunk at 64-token granularity or only emit when boundaries (tool call, fallback) happen.
Kenji: 64-token chunks would still be high volume for very long responses (e.g., batch generation). But it keeps reconstruction precise without per-token events.
Zoe: Another approach: hierarchical provenance where we emit coarse-grain events for every 1k tokens and detailed events only around handoffs (tool-call, fallback, model switch). Then, to audit exact offsets, we replay logs and use KV cache checkpoints to interpolate.
Tam: Tradeoffs: storage + processing complexity vs auditability. Finance SLA says we must be able to explain charges within 24h for any invoice line — not necessarily to show exact token index but to map spend to model/tool and time window.
Marta: So maybe two-tier: billing pipeline consumes compact events with fields {request_id, tenant_id, model_name, token_count, unit_price, time_window}. Separately, raw_provenance stream contains the chunked provenance records for deep audits and dispute resolution.
Priya R: Yes. Implementation notes: runtime will emit small provenance records at model/tool boundaries and every N tokens (configurable N, default 256). Events carry a provenance_id and pointer to request_id + parent_provenance_id. Raw stream is TTLed (e.g., 90 days) or archived to cold storage.
Sam L: For streaming, we need to ensure ordering and determinism for parent_provenance_id assignment. Suggest each runtime instance keeps an incrementing chunk_seq per request and we derive provenance_id = sha256(request_id + chunk_seq + host_id).
Kenji: Good. That avoids UUID generation contention and makes replay deterministic.
Zoe: What about backfills and replays? If we reingest raw_provenance we must avoid double-charging. The compact billing events should be idempotent keyed by ledger_key (tenant_id + request_id + compact_window_start).
Tam: Also we should avoid storing PII in raw_provenance. Strip user prompt text and only keep hashes/pointers.
Marta: Edge case: tool calls that produce tokens attributed to the tool's internal system (like search snippets). We should record tool_owner and tool_cost_code to route to correct charge codes.
Priya R: I sketched an example event we could emit around a fallback boundary:

```json
{ "provenance_id": "p_0001abcd", "request_id": "r_1234", "chunk_seq": "3", "source_type": "model", "model_name": "redwood-ft-16k", "token_count": "200", "start_index": "401", "end_index": "600", "parent_provenance_id": "p_0001ab02" }
```

Sam L: That looks fine. For compact billing a reducer would translate the stream to:

```json
{ "ledger_key": "tenant:xyz|req:r_1234|window:2026-03-21T15:00Z", "model": "redwood-ft-16k", "tokens": "200", "unit_price": "0.0006" }
```

Kenji: One more thing: we need to version the provenance schema (v1, v2) and include schema_version in each event to enable future fields like quantization_level or kernel_tag.
Zoe: Operational questions: how do we surface provenance for customer disputes? An endpoint to stream raw_provenance for a given ledger_key with auth? Or create a replay job that materializes a forensic snapshot.
Tam: Prefer replay job + access control. Direct query against raw stream opens risk of exposing internal metadata and increases attack surface.
Marta: For rollouts we must ensure new runtime changes include a compatibility shim: if provenance not emitted, runtime should still emit a coarse compact event to avoid gaps.
Priya R: Next steps: (1) agree on chunking default (proposal: 256 tokens + boundary emissions) (2) add schema_version and provenance fields (3) implement deterministic provenance_id generation (4) ledger aggregator to idempotently reduce to compact events. Anyone object?
Sam L: +1 on 256 and deterministic ids.
Kenji: +1, also add a config flag to force per-boundary emissions for high-sensitivity tenants.
Zoe: +1. I'll add a note to the RFC follow-up doc about privacy and retention.
Tam: I'll prototype the ingest topology for raw_provenance -> kafka topic -> compact-aggregator service.
eng-deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: provenance-prototype -> staging at 2026-03-21T15:12Z :rocket:
Priya R: Great. I'll update the RFC with the two-tiered approach and the sample schemas, and paste a small checklist. Thanks all.
Sam L: Thanks — will ping if I run into edge cases during prototype.
